root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: `*crl == NULL` after `gnutls_x509_crl_deinit(*crl)` on the CRL-import error path.
root_cause_criterion.criterion: After `gnutls_x509_crl_deinit(*crl)` runs on the CRL-import error path, `gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse()` must clear the caller-owned output slot `*crl` before shared cleanup re-tests it. Otherwise the later cleanup deinit reuses a dangling alias.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable error path frees the newly allocated CRL object and leaves `*crl` non-NULL; the fixed program satisfies the same source-level obligation by storing `NULL` into `*crl` before `goto done`.

nodes.state: Shared cleanup calls `gnutls_x509_crl_deinit(*crl)` with the same stale non-NULL pointer left in the output slot by the earlier error-path deinit, re-entering CRL deinit on freed storage.
The second `gnutls_x509_crl_deinit` entry still receives the freed CRL object as `crl`, and the next `if (crl->crl)` read is the AddressSanitizer-reported heap-use-after-free READ.

edges.relation: The same `*crl` pointer left non-NULL immediately after the error-path deinit later becomes the argument of the shared-cleanup `gnutls_x509_crl_deinit(*crl)` call.
The second cleanup call forwards that same stale CRL pointer into `gnutls_x509_crl_deinit` as its `crl` parameter, carrying the freed receiver directly into the crashing `crl->crl` dereference.
